snippet.textDisplay: It's good that non-Maratha people of India also know about Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj but it's sad and unfortunate that 90% of the mainland Indians still don't have any idea who Lachit Borphukan was. Lachit, the brave Ahom general who defeated the Mughals in the Battle of Saraighat, 1671. The man who who never let Aurangzeb conquer the Northeast, atleast till the time he stayed alive. As an Assamese Lachit Borphukan is our hero like Chatrapati is for the Marathas. Respect for both. "Joi aai okhom"❤

snippet.textDisplay:
खून से लिखी गई ये कहानी है,
संभाजी राजे की अमर निशानी है।
४० दिन तक जो यातनाएँ सही,
हिंदू धर्म की वो बुलंद कहानी है।

ना झुका, ना टूटा, ना धर्म को छोड़ा,
मौत सामने थी, फिर भी नहीं रोड़ा।
हर जख्म पर स्वराज्य लिखा था,
हर पीड़ा में शिवराय दिखा था।

धर्म बचाने को जिसने जीवन दिया,
ऐसे वीर को सतत नमन किया।
आज जो मंदिरों में दीप जलते हैं,
संभाजी राजे की सौगंध चलते हैं।

यूं ही नहीं मिला हमें यह हिंदू धर्म,
किसी की आहुति, किसी का मर्म।
संभाजी राजे ने जो कर दिखाया,
उसका ऋण हर युग ने अपनाया।

जय संभाजी! जय हिंदवी स्वराज्य!

A Hindu asked a muslim - Why the Muslim rulers were killing the Hindus? (Fictional Story from Finland)
It was a chilly spring afternoon in Tampere, but the Tampere University student cafeteria was buzzing with warm conversations and the clinking of cutlery. As usual, Umar and Arun Kumar, both second-year students in Automation Engineering, had found a quiet spot in the corner to have lunch together.
They had become close friends over the past year — sharing jokes, working on class projects, and learning from each other’s cultures. But today, something was off.
Umar noticed it immediately.
"Hey Arun, you alright?" Umar asked, looking up from his tray of rice and vegetables. "You seem quiet. Your face looks a bit tense.”
Arun hesitated for a second, then sighed. “Yeah… something’s bothering me. I wasn’t sure if I should say it.”
“Go ahead, bro. I’m listening,” Umar said calmly.
Arun shifted uncomfortably. “Last night, I watched this Indian historical movie — Chhaava. It shows how Aurangzeb, the Mughal emperor, captured and brutally killed Shambaji, the son of Shivaji. It really disturbed me… I mean, those scenes, the cruelty… I couldn’t sleep.”
Umar listened attentively.
“And?” he asked gently.
“I don’t know, Umar. It made me feel… angry. Like, why did Muslim rulers do that to Hindus?”
Umar nodded slowly. He understood where Arun’s feelings were coming from. And more importantly, he knew this was a moment that required patience, not defensiveness.
“I’m really sorry you felt that way, Arun,” Umar said sincerely. “That must’ve been heavy. But can I share something with you, as a friend?”
Arun nodded.
“First of all,” Umar began, “what you saw in the movie is one version of history — maybe accurate, maybe exaggerated. History is complicated, and it’s often written from a certain perspective. Every side tends to show their version in the best light, and their enemies in the worst. We have to be careful not to judge entire communities based on one version of history.”
Arun leaned in, listening more intently now.
“Secondly,” Umar continued, “just because someone was a Muslim ruler doesn’t mean he acted according to Islam. Islam doesn’t allow cruelty or injustice — not even towards animals, let alone humans. If any ruler, whether Muslim or not, committed injustice, Islam doesn't approve of that.”
Arun frowned slightly. “But what about Aurangzeb?”
Umar nodded. “Good question. There are actually historians who say different things about Aurangzeb. Some portray him as a devout and just ruler, others criticize him for being harsh. The truth is — we weren’t there. We can't be 100% sure of everything that happened.”
He paused, then added, “But even if some of the negative stories are true — we as Muslims don’t take Aurangzeb as our role model. Our example is the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companions, who treated even their enemies with mercy.”
Arun seemed thoughtful. “Hmm... I didn’t know that. I thought Muslims looked up to all the Mughal rulers.”
“Not at all,” Umar replied. “The early caliphs of Islam, like Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab, ruled vast empires, but Christians and Jews lived peacefully under their rule. They had rights, safety, and freedom of worship. That’s the Islamic model of governance — not tyranny.”
He continued, “And think about this — if Aurangzeb really wanted to kill all Hindus, would there be so many Hindus still in India today? Why were there Hindu generals under his rule? Why didn’t he kill them?”
Arun blinked. “You’re saying the wars were about power, not religion?”
“Exactly,” said Umar. “Just like Hindu kings also fought other Hindu kings, and sometimes killed each other — it was about kingdoms, territory, and politics. Not faith.”
There was a long silence at the table. The tension in Arun’s face had eased.
“You know,” he said quietly, “I never thought of it like that. Maybe I was quick to judge.”
Umar smiled. “I understand. We all carry some baggage from the media and stories we hear. But we’re in Finland now — far from the noise. And we’ve got this chance to see each other not as stereotypes, but as people.”
Arun nodded slowly. “You’re right. You’ve always been kind and respectful to me. That speaks louder than any movie.”
“And you’ve been a good friend too,” Umar replied. “Let’s not let the past divide the present. Our job now is to build bridges, not walls.”
That day, something shifted between Arun and Umar — not just friendship, but a deeper respect, a shared understanding, and a quiet commitment to see each other as brothers in humanity.
Moral of the story:
We should never judge a whole community based on the actions of some or the way history is portrayed. Real understanding comes from honest conversations, empathy, and the courage to look beyond stereotypes.

Hindu Mother & Son Conversation

Son: Mom, the Taj Mahal is so beautiful. We built it, right? 🙄

Mom: No, that was also built by Muslim rulers. 🤧

Mom: No dear, the Old Fort was also built by Muslims. 😔

Mom: No. That too was built by Muslim rulers. 😟

Son: Mom, I heard that India created its first missile. That must have been made by Hindu rulers, right? 😀
Mom: No. The first missile in India was developed by Tipu Sultan. He too was a Muslim. 😪

Son: Mom, I heard the Grand Trunk Road is one of the oldest and longest roads in India, almost 3000 kilometers long. We made that, right? 😌
Mom: No, dear. That was also made by a Muslim ruler, Sher Shah Suri. 🙁

Mom: No. That was written by a Muslim poet named Allama Iqbal. 😢

Mom: Well… not exactly. Though Pingali Venkayya designed it, the final recognized version was updated by a Muslim girl named Suraiya Tyabji, from Hyderabad. 😞

Mom: No. Those too were developed by a Muslim—APJ Abdul Kalam. 😭

Son: We at least started the freedom struggle against the British, right??? 😨
Mom: No, the first revolt was started by Tipu Sultan. 😭

Son: So what have we done??? 😤
Declaring cow urine as the ultimate medicine for all ills, I guess? 😭
That's enough now.

Know the real story.

snippet.textDisplay:
Here's a clear, structured History vs. Movie comparison for Chhaava (2025), focusing on key events, characters, and portrayals. The film is inspired by Shivaji Sawant's 1979 novel Chhava (a historical fiction), so it prioritizes dramatic storytelling, patriotism, and emotional impact over strict accuracy. It glorifies Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj as a heroic defender of Swarajya, while portraying Aurangzeb as the ultimate villain.
I've pulled this from historical consensus (e.g., accounts by Jadunath Sarkar, contemporary records, and modern analyses) vs. film depictions and controversies.
Accurate / Mostly Aligned with History
Sambhaji's Capture and Execution (1689): Sambhaji was betrayed near Sangameshwar, captured by Mughal forces, tortured for weeks (including mutilation with wagh nakhe/tiger claws, eyes gouged, tongue cut, limbs torn), refused to convert or surrender forts, and was beheaded. His body was dismembered and thrown in the river. Kavi Kalash suffered similarly. The film's extended torture climax captures the brutality's essence (though possibly toned down for cinema).
Aurangzeb's Orders and Motive: Aurangzeb demanded submission of territories/forts and conversion; refusal led to execution. The death fueled Maratha resistance and prolonged the Deccan wars.
Maratha Guerrilla Tactics & Battles: Hit-and-run style, raids on Mughal supplies (e.g., Burhanpur-inspired scenes) align broadly with Sambhaji's aggressive defense.
Sambhaji's Refusal and Legacy: He refused compromise, earning "Dharamvir" or Swarajya protector status. His reign (1680–1689) focused on resisting Mughal expansion.
Family Dynamics (Broadly): Internal rivalries existed (e.g., with stepmother Soyarabai over succession after Shivaji's death).
Inaccurate / Exaggerated / Fictionalized
Aurangzeb's Personal Involvement: No historical evidence of Aurangzeb meeting Sambhaji face-to-face or overseeing torture in person. He issued orders from afar; dramatic confrontations and dialogues (e.g., "If Sambhaji were with me...") are invented for cinematic tension.
Shirke Family Betrayal (Ganoji/Kanhoji Shirke): Film shows them as traitors aiding capture. Descendants protested (threatened ₹100 crore lawsuit, demanded apologies), claiming no solid proof—some sources blame court scribes or others. Director called it fiction-inspired; family argued Yesubai (Sambhaji's wife) was from Shirke clan, making betrayal unlikely. This is one of the biggest controversies.
Soyarabai's Portrayal: Shown conspiring openly with Mughals, sitting in durbar eating paan. No strong evidence for direct Mughal alliance or such public behavior; succession plots existed but exaggerated.
Dramatic Action Scenes: Sambhaji emerging from water/mud in battles, superhuman feats, or personal single-handed charges in every fight—pure Bollywood flair. Burhanpur raid is amplified for spectacle.
"Shiv Garjana" & Chants: Signature roars or specific "Shiv Garjana" aren't historically documented as his thing; "Har Har Mahadev" wasn't uniquely his battle cry like shown.
Simplified Binary Narrative: Heavy Hindu vs. Muslim/Indian vs. Foreigner framing. Reality was complex—Sambhaji briefly defected to Mughals (imprisoned by Shivaji for it), alliances shifted (Aurangzeb had many Hindu mansabdars, up to 33% in admin), Marathas sometimes raided civilians. Film whitewashes Sambhaji's ruthless side (e.g., executing ministers) and omits nuances like caste tensions or political motives over pure religious ones for torture.
Other Minor Additions: Sambhaji allying against Mughals in certain dialogues (ignoring his past defection), exaggerated heroism making him seem invincible.
Overall Verdict
Chhaava is more grounded than many Bollywood historicals (sticks to broad timeline of Sambhaji's life, capture, and death), revives his legacy powerfully (he's often less celebrated than Shivaji), and nails the emotional patriotism. But it's loaded with creative liberties for mass appeal—exaggerations, inventions, and a one-sided good-vs-evil lens that sparked backlash (Shirke protests, debates on Wikipedia edits, political polarization). Historians call it propaganda-ish for skipping complexities and aligning with modern narratives.

Maratha Guerrilla Tactics & Battles: Hit-and-run style, raids on Mughal supplies (e.g., Burhanpur-inspired scenes) align broadly with Sambhaji's aggressive defense.
Sambhaji's Refusal and Legacy: He refused compromise, earning "Dharamvir" or Swarajya protector status. His reign (1680–1689) focused on resisting Mughal expansion.
Family Dynamics (Broadly): Internal rivalries existed (e.g., with stepmother Soyarabai over succession after Shivaji's death).
Inaccurate / Exaggerated / Fictionalized
Aurangzeb's Personal Involvement: No historical evidence of Aurangzeb meeting Sambhaji face-to-face or overseeing torture in person. He issued orders from afar; dramatic confrontations and dialogues (e.g., "If Sambhaji were with me...") are invented for cinematic tension.
Shirke Family Betrayal (Ganoji/Kanhoji Shirke): Film shows them as traitors aiding capture. Descendants protested (threatened ₹100 crore lawsuit, demanded apologies), claiming no solid proof—some sources blame court scribes or others. Director called it fiction-inspired; family argued Yesubai (Sambhaji's wife) was from Shirke clan, making betrayal unlikely. This is one of the biggest controversies.
Soyarabai's Portrayal: Shown conspiring openly with Mughals, sitting in durbar eating paan. No strong evidence for direct Mughal alliance or such public behavior; succession plots existed but exaggerated.
Dramatic Action Scenes: Sambhaji emerging from water/mud in battles, superhuman feats, or personal single-handed charges in every fight—pure Bollywood flair. Burhanpur raid is amplified for spectacle.
"Shiv Garjana" & Chants: Signature roars or specific "Shiv Garjana" aren't historically documented as his thing; "Har Har Mahadev" wasn't uniquely his battle cry like shown.
Simplified Binary Narrative: Heavy Hindu vs. Muslim/Indian vs. Foreigner framing. Reality was complex—Sambhaji briefly defected to Mughals (imprisoned by Shivaji for it), alliances shifted (Aurangzeb had many Hindu mansabdars, up to 33% in admin), Marathas sometimes raided civilians. Film whitewashes Sambhaji's ruthless side (e.g., executing ministers) and omits nuances like caste tensions or political motives over pure religious ones for torture.
Other Minor Additions: Sambhaji allying against Mughals in certain dialogues (ignoring his past defection), exaggerated heroism making him seem invincible.
Overall Verdict
Chhaava is more grounded than many Bollywood historicals (sticks to broad timeline of Sambhaji's life, capture, and death), revives his legacy powerfully (he's often less celebrated than Shivaji), and nails the emotional patriotism. But it's loaded with creative liberties for mass appeal—exaggerations, inventions, and a one-sided good-vs-evil lens that sparked backlash (Shirke protests, debates on Wikipedia edits, political polarization). Historians call it propaganda-ish for skipping complexities and aligning with modern narratives.

snippet.textDisplay:
पहला, 'लव जिहाद' एक आधारहीन सिद्धांत है, जो दावा करता है कि मुस्लिम पुरुष हिंदू महिलाओं का धर्म परिवर्तन कराने के लिए उनके साथ प्रेम संबंध बनाते हैं। विभिन्न जांचों में यह सिद्धांत गलत साबित हुआ है और यह समाज में विभाजन और नफरत पैदा करता है। ​
इसके अलावा, 'हलाल' पद्धति के बारे में साजिश सिद्धांत मुस्लिम खाद्य प्रसंस्करण प्रथाओं और आर्थिक असमानता पैदा करने के प्रयासों को गलत तरीके से प्रस्तुत करता है। ऐसे सिद्धांत निराधार हैं और समाज में नफरत फैलाने के लिए इस्तेमाल किये जाते हैं। ​
हिजाब पर प्रतिबंध और कर्नाटक राज्य में शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में हाल की हिंसा समाज में धार्मिक अल्पसंख्यकों को प्रभावित कर रही है। ऐसे में सभी समुदायों के बीच सद्भाव और सहिष्णुता स्थापित करना बहुत जरूरी है
भारत में मुस्लिम और ईसाई समुदायों के खिलाफ झूठी सूचना और हिंसा फैलाने के लिए जिम्मेदार लोगों को न्याय के कटघरे में लाया जाना चाहिए। उदाहरण के लिए, बाबरी मस्जिद विध्वंस, 2002 के गुजरात दंगे, 2006 के मालेगांव विस्फोट, बुल्ली बाई और सुल्ली सौदे के मामलों के लिए जिम्मेदार लोगों को दंडित किया जाना चाहिए। साथ ही, नागरिकता (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 और हरिद्वार घृणा भाषण मुद्दों पर न्याय लाना महत्वपूर्ण है। यहां तक ​​कि, कुछ हिंदुत्व गायकों और मीडिया संगठनों के खिलाफ उनकी घृणित गतिविधियों के लिए कार्रवाई की जानी चाहिए
सबसे बढ़कर, समाज में शांति और सद्भाव स्थापित करने के लिए सभी समुदायों के बीच सद्भाव और सहिष्णुता को बढ़ावा देना चाहिए। साथ ही, सभी को झूठे सिद्धांतों और घृणा प्रचार के खिलाफ जागरूक होना चाहिए और न्याय के लिए समर्थन करना चाहिए।

snippet.textDisplay:
मुसलमानों से बुरी तरह पिटे हुए लोगों को हीरो बना कर पेश करना यानि झूठ को सच दिखाना बोली वुड का ही काम है।
भारत के दुश्मनों के व्यू ऑफ पॉइंट से ये काम अच्छा है। क्योंकि ऐसे भारत तकसीम होता है। भारतीयों को शायद ये बात अजीब लगे मगर हक़ीक़त में कुछ यूं है कि इस क़िसम की फिल्में वास्तव में भारत को तोड़ने का एजेंडा है। क्योंकि ये अमरीकियों का पुराना एजेंडा है कि अगर किसी देश को तोड़ना है तो पहले उस के अंदर तकसीम पैदा करो। उस देश में रहने वाली जनता और मुख्तलिफ समुदाय कोे आपस में लड़वा दो। और फिर सकून से बैठ कर इन की बर्बादी और टूटने का नज़ारा देखो। भारत में भी ऐसा ही कुछ हो रहा है।
अमरीका ने जैसे १९८० के दशक में पाकिस्तान के अंदर इस्लामाइजेशन पर ज़ोर दिया और इस्लामिक जेहाद के जरिए रूस को अफगानिस्तान से निकाला और फिर पाकिस्तान ने इन्हीं मुजाहिदीन की मदद से अमरीकियों को अफगानिस्तान से निकाला। बिल्कुल इसी तरीके भारत में अपलाई किया जा रहा है।
भारत के अंदर धर्म के नाम पे आम लोगों और जवानों को इकठ्ठा कर के सी आई ए की मदद से चीन को तोड़ना है। 
जबकि अमरीका ये नहीं जनता की अमरीका के मंसूबे से पहले उसे भांप कर स्विंग तेज़ी से साउथ एशिया समेत पूरी दुनिया के मुसलमानों को अपने साथ मिला चुका है। साउथ एशिया के सिर्फ तीन देशों यानि भारत, पाकिस्तान और बांग्लादेश में तकरीबन ६५ करोड़ से जायेद मुसलमान बस्ते हैं। 
और मुसलमानों के सब से बड़ा हथियार जेहाद है इस के आगे तमाम हथियार बेकार हैं।
यही वजह है कि अब की बार अगर किसी ने धार्मिक एडवेंचर किया तो वो पृथ्वी राज चौहान से भी ज़्यादा बुरे इंजन से दोचार होगा।

snippet.textDisplay:
छत्रपति संभाजी महाराज 

वीरता का अवतार थे, वीर संभाजी महाराज,  
शिवाजी के रक्त का, वो महान अनुयायी राज।  
साहस और बलिदान का, उन्होंने इतिहास रचा,  
संग्राम की राह पर, हर कष्ट को उन्होंने सहा।

धर्म, संस्कृति और स्वराज की रक्षा के लिए,  
निरंतर संघर्ष करते रहे, वो वीर सपूत सच्चे।  
मुठी भर सेनाओं से, मुगलों को हराया,  
अपने तीर-तलवार से, शत्रु को हर समय हराया।

सिंहासन की अहमियत नहीं, उन्हें थी मातृभूमि प्यारी,  
स्वतंत्रता की खातिर, वो झूले नहीं, थे तैयार हर क़ीमत चुकाने।  
अपने अधिकारों की रक्षा में, जान दी थी उन्होंने,  
कभी भी नहीं झुके थे, हार से अडिग खड़े थे वो हमेशा।

उनकी क़ुर्बानी, उनके साहस की मिसाल बन गई,  
स्वराज की मूरत, आज भी हर दिल में बस गई।  
संभाजी महाराज, इतिहास में अमर हो गए,  
उनकी वीरता की गाथाएँ, हमे सिखातीं हैं सही रास्ता देने।

**जय संभाजी महाराज!**🙌🙌🙌

snippet.textDisplay:
Almost after 40 days of release finally last night i have watched this legendary historic movie  in Goregaon east miraj cinemas.
I wanted to watch this movie since it was released but i was too busy and not getting free time because of my academic responsibilities and  theater also is just 50 meter away from my home but still i couldn't watch it. Thankfully yesterday i got a free so i watched in last show at 10:30PM and that too i've seen this movie alone which is first time ever happened in my life till now.
Now i'd like to say thay this is not a movie but it's our history we must do not forget who were our "Dev Tulya Warriors" who faught for are pride and protected our culture and dharma from foreign cruel jih@di invaders.
I cannot enough appreciate the level of acting did Vicky kaushal and portrayed  the character of shri chhatrapati "Shambhu Raje Ji Maharaj" in this movie every actor has done justice with every legendary character of our warriors and director Utekar also deserves huge applaud for his direction. 
Last i'd like to say even after 40 days later  it's release in last show there was more than 60% occupancy in the theater it show how much this movie has became popular among the people.

पोस्ट पूरी पढ़ना ज़रूर==

जब मुगलों ने पूरे भारत को एक किया तो इस देश का नाम कोई इस्लामिक नहीं बल्कि "हिन्दुस्तान" रखा , हाँलाकि इस्लामिक नाम भी रख सकते थे !
कौन विरोध करता ?

जिनको इलाहाबाद और फैजाबाद चुभता है वह समझ लें कि मुगलों के ही दौर में "रामपुर" बना रहा तो "सीतापुर" भी बना रहा!

अयोध्या तो बसा ही मुगलों के दौर में !

आज के वातावरण में मुगलों को सोचता हूँ और मुस्लिम शासकों को सोचता हूँ तो लगता है कि उन्होंने मुर्खता की!

होशियार तो ग्वालियर का सिंधिया घराना था!
होशियार तो मैसूर का वाडियार घराना था!
होशियार तो जयपुर का राजशाही घराना था!
होशियार तो जोधपुर का भी राजघराना था!
टीपू सुल्तान हो या बहादुरशाह ज़फर शायद यह सब बेवकूफ लोग थे, जो अपने मुल्क़ के लिए चिथड़े चिथड़े हो गए, किसी को देश की मिट्टी भी नसीब नहीं हुई और आज इन सबके वंशज भीख माँग रहे हैं!*

अँग्रेजों से मिल जाते तो वह भी अपने महल बचा लेते और अपनी रियासतें बचा लेते!*
वाडियार, जयपुर, जोधपुर, और सिंधिया राजघराने की तरह उनके भी वंशज आज ऐश करते!*
उनकी औलादें भी आज मंत्री और मुख्यमंत्री बनते!

यह आज का दौर है यहाँ "भारत माता की जय" और "वंदेमातरम" कहने से ही इंसान देशभक्त हो जाता है, चाहें उसका इतिहास देश से गद्दारी का ही क्युँ ना हो!

बहादुर शाह ज़फर ने जब 1857 के गदर में अँग्रैजों के खिलाफ़ पूरे देश का नेतृत्व किया और उनको पूरे देश के राजा रजवाड़ों तथा बादशाहों ने अपना नेता माना!
भीषण लड़ाई के बाद अंग्रेजों की छल कपट नीति से बहादुरशाह ज़फर पराजित हुए और गिरफ्तार कर लिए गये!

ब्रिटिश कैद में जब बहादुर शाह जफर को भूख लगी तो अंग्रेज उनके सामने थाली में परोसकर उनके बेटों के कटे हुए सिर लेकर आए!
उन्होंने अंग्रेजों को जवाब दिया कि "हिंदुस्तान के बेटे अपने देश के लिए सिर कुर्बान करके अपने बाप के पास इसी अंदाज में आया करते हैं"!

शायद बेवकूफ़ थे बहादुरशाह ज़फर, जिन्होंने अपने मुल्क़ के लिए खुद को और अपने जवान बेटों को कुरबान कर दिया, और आज उसका नतीजा कि उनकी औलादें भीख माँग कर गुज़ारा कर रहे हैं!

अपने मुल्क़ हिन्दुस्तान की ज़मीन में दफन होने की उनकी चाह भी पूरी ना हो सकी और रंगून के कैदखाने में ही अपनी आखिरी सांस ली, और फिर वर्मा की मिट्टी में दफन कर दिए गये!

अंग्रेजों ने उनकी कब्र की निशानी भी ना छोड़ी और मिट्टी बराबर करके फसल उगा दी, बाद में एक खुदाई में उनका वहीं से कंकाल मिला और फिर शिनाख्त के बाद उनकी क़ब्र बनाई गयी!

सोचिए कि आज "बहादुरशाह ज़फर" को कौन याद करता है ?
क्या मिला उनको देश के लिए अपने खानदान की कुर्बानी से ?
7 नवंबर 1862 को उनकी मौत हुई थी!
लेकिन क्या किसी ने कभी उनको श्रृद्धान्जली भी दी ?

जब मुगलों ने पूरे भारत को एक किया तो इस देश का नाम कोई इस्लामिक नहीं बल्कि "हिन्दुस्तान" रखा , हाँलाकि इस्लामिक नाम भी रख सकते थे !
कौन विरोध करता ?

जिनको इलाहाबाद और फैजाबाद चुभता है वह समझ लें कि मुगलों के ही दौर में "रामपुर" बना रहा तो "सीतापुर" भी बना रहा!

अयोध्या तो बसा ही मुगलों के दौर में !

आज के वातावरण में मुगलों को सोचता हूँ और मुस्लिम शासकों को सोचता हूँ तो लगता है कि उन्होंने मुर्खता की!

होशियार तो ग्वालियर का सिंधिया घराना था!
होशियार तो मैसूर का वाडियार घराना था!
होशियार तो जयपुर का राजशाही घराना था!
होशियार तो जोधपुर का भी राजघराना था!
टीपू सुल्तान हो या बहादुरशाह ज़फर शायद यह सब बेवकूफ लोग थे, जो अपने मुल्क़ के लिए चिथड़े चिथड़े हो गए, किसी को देश की मिट्टी भी नसीब नहीं हुई और आज इन सबके वंशज भीख माँग रहे हैं!*

अँग्रेजों से मिल जाते तो वह भी अपने महल बचा लेते और अपनी रियासतें बचा लेते!*
वाडियार, जयपुर, जोधपुर, और सिंधिया राजघराने की तरह उनके भी वंशज आज ऐश करते!*
उनकी औलादें भी आज मंत्री और मुख्यमंत्री बनते!

यह आज का दौर है यहाँ "भारत माता की जय" और "वंदेमातरम" कहने से ही इंसान देशभक्त हो जाता है, चाहें उसका इतिहास देश से गद्दारी का ही क्युँ ना हो!

भीषण लड़ाई के बाद अंग्रेजों की छल कपट नीति से बहादुरशाह ज़फर पराजित हुए और गिरफ्तार कर लिए गये!

उन्होंने अंग्रेजों को जवाब दिया कि "हिंदुस्तान के बेटे अपने देश के लिए सिर कुर्बान करके अपने बाप के पास इसी अंदाज में आया करते हैं"!

अपने मुल्क़ हिन्दुस्तान की ज़मीन में दफन होने की उनकी चाह भी पूरी ना हो सकी और रंगून के कैदखाने में ही अपनी आखिरी सांस ली, और फिर वर्मा की मिट्टी में दफन कर दिए गये!

अंग्रेजों ने उनकी कब्र की निशानी भी ना छोड़ी और मिट्टी बराबर करके फसल उगा दी, बाद में एक खुदाई में उनका वहीं से कंकाल मिला और फिर शिनाख्त के बाद उनकी क़ब्र बनाई गयी!

This is the *classic cycle* —keep people emotionally charged over history, religion, and identity, while *real-life issues like jobs, healthcare, and education remain ignored*. Bollywood, just like politicians, plays into this because *controversy sells*.  

- Instead of making movies about *real-life problems* (poverty, unemployment, farmer suicides, pollution, education crisis), they *rehash historical conflicts*.  
- Movies like "Chhaava" aren’t just about storytelling; they serve *political agendas*, reinforcing a *"us vs. them"* mindset.  
- The audience, instead of questioning *rising costs, bad infrastructure, or lack of healthcare*, gets *emotionally invested in glorifying or vilifying past rulers*.  

It’s exactly what BJP does before every election—*fueling Hindu-Muslim sentiments*, renaming places, talking about temples while ignoring real issues. And Bollywood directors? *They follow the same formula because it guarantees attention, protests, and ticket sales*.  

If people *stopped falling for these distractions* and *demanded accountability*, neither politicians nor filmmakers could keep playing these games. But as long as the public *chooses emotional battles over real-world struggles*, this cycle will continue.
*JAI HIND*

छत्रपति संभाजी महाराज 

वीरता का अवतार थे, वीर संभाजी महाराज,  
शिवाजी के रक्त का, वो महान अनुयायी राज।  
साहस और बलिदान का, उन्होंने इतिहास रचा,  
संग्राम की राह पर, हर कष्ट को उन्होंने सहा।

धर्म, संस्कृति और स्वराज की रक्षा के लिए,  
निरंतर संघर्ष करते रहे, वो वीर सपूत सच्चे।  
मुठी भर सेनाओं से, मुगलों को हराया,  
अपने तीर-तलवार से, शत्रु को हर समय हराया।

सिंहासन की अहमियत नहीं, उन्हें थी मातृभूमि प्यारी,  
स्वतंत्रता की खातिर, वो झूले नहीं, थे तैयार हर क़ीमत चुकाने।  
अपने अधिकारों की रक्षा में, जान दी थी उन्होंने,  
कभी भी नहीं झुके थे, हार से अडिग खड़े थे वो हमेशा।

उनकी क़ुर्बानी, उनके साहस की मिसाल बन गई,  
स्वराज की मूरत, आज भी हर दिल में बस गई।  
संभाजी महाराज, इतिहास में अमर हो गए,  
उनकी वीरता की गाथाएँ, हमे सिखातीं हैं सही रास्ता देने।

**जय संभाजी महाराज!**🙌🙌🙌

snippet.textDisplay: Genuine Review. There was so much hype so i watched tis movie. But it was average. The last scene inspired by RRR movie and some part from BajiRao Mastani. Very easy job for director. Vicky kaushal was shouting "ahhhhhh" during entire movie. Action scene was weak and without logic,like vicky kaushal was tied with chain for aprox 2 or 3 days but his blood in entire body was fresh instead it should be dried up, simple logic. Standing firm for 2 to 3 days in same position doesn't make sense,which shows lack in direction. Vicky kaushal fighting and talking with his associate during fight scene, how is it possible? snippet.textDisplay:
Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, remains a figure of intense historical debate.
His reign, the longest of the Mughals, saw the empire reach its greatest territorial extent.
However, his strict adherence to Islamic law alienated many of his non-Muslim subjects.
His policies, including the reimposition of the Jizya tax, fueled religious tensions.
Military campaigns in the Deccan drained the empire's resources and contributed to its decline.
He was a complex figure, both a skilled administrator and a controversial ruler.
His legacy continues to be a subject of scholarly discussion and differing interpretations.
Ultimately, his reign marked a turning point in Mughal history.

snippet.textDisplay:
भाई चावा या चित्रपटात खूप कमी भाग दाखवला आहे, त्यातही खूप भाग कमी करण्यात आला आहे, जसे की - 

1) संभाजी महाराजांनी कधी नाशिक/नागपूर, जालना यांसारख्या शहरांचे नाव घेतलेले नाही, कारण त्या वेळेला ते सद्दाम आणि डेक्कनमध्ये विभागले गेले होते. 

2) औरंगजेबच्या मुलीला संभाजी महाराजांवर प्रेम झाले होते त्यांच्या शौर्यतेमुळे, आणि जर त्यांनी त्यांच्याशी विवाह केला असता, तर आज ते वाचले असते. 

3) संभाजी महाराज औरंगजेबच्या कैदेत 40-45 दिवस होते आणि रोज त्यांना वेगवेगळ्या ठिकाणी नेले जाईल, त्यामुळे मराठ्यांना त्यांच्या स्थानाची माहिती मिळू नये. 

4) त्यांच्या डोळ्यांचा भाग चित्रपटात खूप लवकर निघाला, पण तसा नाही, त्यांचे डोळे साधारण 30 दिवसांनी निघाले होते. 

ही माहिती मला इतर पुस्तकांमधून वाचून सापडली आहे, तरी काही चुकले असेल तर माफी. 🙏🏻🧡

snippet.textDisplay:
Bollywood’s Dangerous Game with History
The Indian film industry has once again proven that it is not merely about entertainment but a powerful tool for shaping public perception—often at the cost of truth. The movie Chhava is yet another example of Bollywood distorting history, portraying Emperor Aurangzeb in an excessively negative light. Such deliberate misrepresentation is not just an attack on historical facts but a reckless provocation that risks inflaming ethnic and religious tensions in a country already struggling with communal harmony.

India, which prides itself on being the world's largest democracy, is playing with fire by promoting narratives that divide rather than unite. Muslims, the second-largest community in the country, have played an undeniable role in its economic, cultural, and social progress. Yet, time and again, they are subjected to demonization in mainstream cinema—fueling prejudice and deepening societal rifts.

This is not just about a film; it is about mind-shaping propaganda disguised as entertainment. By pushing selective narratives, Bollywood seems to be operating with a deeper agenda—one that benefits from division rather than unity. The consequences of such distortions are far from trivial. We have seen how communal riots have erupted time and again due to politically charged rhetoric and inflammatory portrayals. Instead of learning from the past, the industry appears determined to repeat history, sowing the seeds of discord that could once again lead to violence and unrest.

The question is: Who benefits from this narrative? Certainly not the common people of India, who deserve films that promote understanding rather than hostility. If Bollywood continues down this path, it will not only damage its own credibility but also push India further into a cycle of internal strife. Responsible storytelling is a duty, not an option, and it is high time the industry realizes the weight of its influence before it’s too late.

snippet.textDisplay:
🔴Please , this is a serious note ....try to read everything I wrote: 
It’s absolutely outrageous how Indian history books have been designed to glorify foreign revolutions and rulers while completely sidelining the true heroes of our own land! Why on earth are students being forced to learn about the French Revolution, the Russian Revolution, and foreign figures like Hitler, Napoleon, and Louis IX instead of our own warriors who sacrificed everything for this nation?

The worst part is, our textbooks seem obsessed with the stories of Mughal rulers like Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Akbar, Babar, Alauddin Khilji, Aurangzeb, and Tipu Sultan, presenting them as if they were the only ones who shaped India’s history. But what about our own kings — the Marathas, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj, Prithviraj Chauhan, Chandragupta Maurya, and countless others who fought bravely to protect this land and uphold Hindu traditions? Their stories of valor, resistance, and sacrifice deserve to be at the forefront of our history books, not buried beneath chapters glorifying invaders and foreign events!

Is it any wonder that more than half of India’s population doesn’t truly respect or understand the depth of Hindu culture and history? Our royal kings laid down their lives resisting forced conversions and defending this land's religion and culture. But our education system seems hell-bent on ensuring that students know more about Europe’s past than their own!

It’s infuriating that if not for a few patriotic filmmakers and storytellers who dared to bring these legends to the big screen, our generation and even our parents would have remained ignorant of our own history. Is this a deliberate attempt to erase our legacy? Why is the government so focused on teaching us everything except India’s real history?

If students are being taught history, then why not our own? Why are we gathering information about countries that don’t even care about India? It’s high time we demand history books that celebrate our warriors, our culture, and our sacrifices! Enough of this bias — we want Indian history for Indian students!

snippet.textDisplay:
মারাঠা সাম্রাজ্য নিয়ে আজীবন গবেষক ঐতিহাসিক যদুনাথ সরকার তাঁর শিবাজী গ্রন্থে বলছেন : 
শিবাজীর জ্যেষ্ঠপুত্র শম্ভুজী যেন পিতার পাপের ফল হইয়া জন্মিয়া ছিলেন। এই একুশ বৎসর বয়সেই তিনি উদ্ধত, খামখেয়ালি, নেশাখোর এবং লম্পট হইয়া পড়িয়াছেন। একজন সধবা ব্রাহ্মণীর ধর্ম নষ্ট করিবার ফলে ন্যায়পরায়ণ পিতার আদেশে তাঁহাকে পনহালা দুর্গে আবদ্ধ করিয়া রাখা হয়। সেখান হইতে শম্ভুজী নিজ স্ত্রী যেসু বাঈকে সঙ্গে লইয়া গোপনে পলাইয়া গিয়া দিলির খাঁ'র সহিত যোগ দিলেন (১৩ই ডিসেম্বর, ১৬৭৮)। শম্ভুজীকে পাইয়া দিলির খাঁর আহ্লাদ ধরে না। "তিনি যেন ইতিমধ্যে সমস্ত দাক্ষিণাত্য জয় করিয়াছেন এরূপ উল্লাস করিতে লাগিলেন এবং বাদশাহকে এই পরম সুখবর দিলেন।” আওরংজীবের পক্ষ হইতে শম্ভুজীকে সাত হাজারী মনসব, রাজা উপাধি এবং একটি হাতী দেওয়া হইল। তাহার পর দুজনে একসঙ্গে বিজাপুর দখল করিতে চলিলেন।

তাহার পর শম্ভুজীকে সঙ্গে লইয়া দিলির খাঁ শিবাজীর ভুপালগড় তোপের জোরে কাড়িয়া লইলেন, এবং এখানে প্রচুর শস্য, ধন, মালপত্র, এবং অনেক লোককে ধরিলেন। এই সব বন্দীদের কতকগুলির এক হাত কাটিয়া ছাড়িয়া দেওয়া হইল, অবশিষ্ট সকলকে দাস করিয়া বিক্রয় করা হইল (২রা এপ্রিল, ১৬৭৯)। ঐ দুর্গের দেওয়াল ও বুরুজগুলি ভাঙ্গিয়া দেওয়া হইল।

বিজাপুরের মত প্রবল এবং বৃহৎ দুর্গ জয় করা দিলিরের কাজ নহে; স্বয়ং জয়সিংহও এখানে বিফল হইয়াছিলেন। একমাস সময় নষ্ট করিয়া ১৪ই নভেম্বর দিলির বিজাপুর শহর হইতে সরিয়া গিয়া তাহার পশ্চিমের ধনশালী নগর ও গ্রামগুলি লুঠিতে আরম্ভ করিলেন। এই অঞ্চল যে মুঘলেরা আক্রমণ করিবে তাহা কেহই ভাবে নাই, কারণ মুঘলদিগের পশ্চাতে রাজধানী তখনও অপরাজিত ছিল। সুতরাং এই দিক হইতে লোকে পলায় নাই, স্ত্রী পুত্র ধন নিরাপদ স্থানে সরায় নাই। এই অপ্রস্তুত অবস্থায় শত্রুর হাতে পড়িয়া তাহাদের কঠোর দুর্দশা হইল। "হিন্দু ও মুসলমান স্ত্রীলোকগণ সন্তান বুকে ধরিয়া বাড়ির কুয়ায় ঝাঁপাইয়া পড়িয়া সতীত্ব রক্ষা করিল। গ্রামকে গ্রাম লুঠে উজাড় হইল। একটি বড় গ্রামে তিন হাজার হিন্দু মুসলমান (অনেকে নিকটবর্তী ছোট গ্রাম-গুলির পলাতক আশ্রয়প্রার্থী)-দের দাসরূপে বিক্রয় করিয়া দেওয়া হইল।"

 শম্ভুজী পনহালাতে ফিরিয়া আসায় (৪ঠা ডিসেম্বর), শিবাজী স্বয়ং সেই দুর্গে জানুয়ারির প্রথমে গেলেন। জ্যেষ্ঠপুত্রের চরিত্র ও বুদ্ধির কথা ভাবিয়া শিবাজী নিজ রাজ্য ও বংশের ভবিষ্যৎ সম্বন্ধে হতাশ হইলেন। তাঁহার নানা উপদেশ ও মিষ্ট কথায় কোন ফল হইস না। শিবাজী পুত্রকে নিজের বিশাল রাজ্যের সমস্ত মহাল দুর্গ ধনভাণ্ডার অশ্ব গজ ও সৈন্যদলের তালিকা দেখাইলেন এবং সৎ ও উচ্চমনা রাজা হইবার জন্য নানা উপদেশ দিলেন। শম্ভুজী পিতার কথা শুধু চুপ করিয়া শুনিয়া উত্তর দিলেন, "আপনার যাহা ইচ্ছা তাহাই হউক।” শিবাজী স্পষ্টই বুঝিলেন তাঁহার মৃত্যুর পর শম্ভুজীর হাতে মহারাষ্ট্র রাজ্যের কি দশা হইবে। এই দুর্ভাবনা ও হতাশা তাঁহার আয়ু হ্রাস করিল। শম্ভুজীকে আবার পনহালা-দুর্গে বন্দী করিয়া রাখা হইল, এবং শিবাজী রায়গড়ে ফিরিয়া আসিলেন (ফেব্রুয়ারি ১৬৮০)। তাঁহার দিন ফুরাইয়া আসিয়াছে বুঝিয়া, শিবাজী তাড়াতাডি কনিষ্ঠ পুত্র – দশ বৎসরের বালক রাজারামের উপবীত ও বিবাহ দিলেন (৭ই ও ১৫ই মার্চ)।
(সূত্র "শিবাজী" : যদুনাথ সরকার)

এখন এমন চরিত্রের মানুষ, যাকে তার পিতা পর্যন্ত ভরসা করেন নাই, দুইবার বন্দি করেছেন, দেশবাসী তাকে স্মরণ করে আহা উহু করবে, নাকি দেশের স্বাধীনতা আন্দোলনের বীর বিপ্লবী ক্ষুদিরাম, আসফাকুল্লাহ খান, সূর্য সেন, ভগৎ সিং, উধম সিং, সুভাষ চন্দ্র বসুর মত মানুষদের স্মরণ করে তাদের পথের পথিক হবে, তার ভাবনা সম্পূর্ণ তাদের উপরেই থাকল।

মারাঠা সাম্রাজ্য নিয়ে আজীবন গবেষক ঐতিহাসিক যদুনাথ সরকার তাঁর শিবাজী গ্রন্থে বলছেন : 
শিবাজীর জ্যেষ্ঠপুত্র শম্ভুজী যেন পিতার পাপের ফল হইয়া জন্মিয়া ছিলেন। এই একুশ বৎসর বয়সেই তিনি উদ্ধত, খামখেয়ালি, নেশাখোর এবং লম্পট হইয়া পড়িয়াছেন। একজন সধবা ব্রাহ্মণীর ধর্ম নষ্ট করিবার ফলে ন্যায়পরায়ণ পিতার আদেশে তাঁহাকে পনহালা দুর্গে আবদ্ধ করিয়া রাখা হয়। সেখান হইতে শম্ভুজী নিজ স্ত্রী যেসু বাঈকে সঙ্গে লইয়া গোপনে পলাইয়া গিয়া দিলির খাঁ'র সহিত যোগ দিলেন (১৩ই ডিসেম্বর, ১৬৭৮)। শম্ভুজীকে পাইয়া দিলির খাঁর আহ্লাদ ধরে না। "তিনি যেন ইতিমধ্যে সমস্ত দাক্ষিণাত্য জয় করিয়াছেন এরূপ উল্লাস করিতে লাগিলেন এবং বাদশাহকে এই পরম সুখবর দিলেন।” আওরংজীবের পক্ষ হইতে শম্ভুজীকে সাত হাজারী মনসব, রাজা উপাধি এবং একটি হাতী দেওয়া হইল। তাহার পর দুজনে একসঙ্গে বিজাপুর দখল করিতে চলিলেন।

তাহার পর শম্ভুজীকে সঙ্গে লইয়া দিলির খাঁ শিবাজীর ভুপালগড় তোপের জোরে কাড়িয়া লইলেন, এবং এখানে প্রচুর শস্য, ধন, মালপত্র, এবং অনেক লোককে ধরিলেন। এই সব বন্দীদের কতকগুলির এক হাত কাটিয়া ছাড়িয়া দেওয়া হইল, অবশিষ্ট সকলকে দাস করিয়া বিক্রয় করা হইল (২রা এপ্রিল, ১৬৭৯)। ঐ দুর্গের দেওয়াল ও বুরুজগুলি ভাঙ্গিয়া দেওয়া হইল।

বিজাপুরের মত প্রবল এবং বৃহৎ দুর্গ জয় করা দিলিরের কাজ নহে; স্বয়ং জয়সিংহও এখানে বিফল হইয়াছিলেন। একমাস সময় নষ্ট করিয়া ১৪ই নভেম্বর দিলির বিজাপুর শহর হইতে সরিয়া গিয়া তাহার পশ্চিমের ধনশালী নগর ও গ্রামগুলি লুঠিতে আরম্ভ করিলেন। এই অঞ্চল যে মুঘলেরা আক্রমণ করিবে তাহা কেহই ভাবে নাই, কারণ মুঘলদিগের পশ্চাতে রাজধানী তখনও অপরাজিত ছিল। সুতরাং এই দিক হইতে লোকে পলায় নাই, স্ত্রী পুত্র ধন নিরাপদ স্থানে সরায় নাই। এই অপ্রস্তুত অবস্থায় শত্রুর হাতে পড়িয়া তাহাদের কঠোর দুর্দশা হইল। "হিন্দু ও মুসলমান স্ত্রীলোকগণ সন্তান বুকে ধরিয়া বাড়ির কুয়ায় ঝাঁপাইয়া পড়িয়া সতীত্ব রক্ষা করিল। গ্রামকে গ্রাম লুঠে উজাড় হইল। একটি বড় গ্রামে তিন হাজার হিন্দু মুসলমান (অনেকে নিকটবর্তী ছোট গ্রাম-গুলির পলাতক আশ্রয়প্রার্থী)-দের দাসরূপে বিক্রয় করিয়া দেওয়া হইল।"

 শম্ভুজী পনহালাতে ফিরিয়া আসায় (৪ঠা ডিসেম্বর), শিবাজী স্বয়ং সেই দুর্গে জানুয়ারির প্রথমে গেলেন। জ্যেষ্ঠপুত্রের চরিত্র ও বুদ্ধির কথা ভাবিয়া শিবাজী নিজ রাজ্য ও বংশের ভবিষ্যৎ সম্বন্ধে হতাশ হইলেন। তাঁহার নানা উপদেশ ও মিষ্ট কথায় কোন ফল হইস না। শিবাজী পুত্রকে নিজের বিশাল রাজ্যের সমস্ত মহাল দুর্গ ধনভাণ্ডার অশ্ব গজ ও সৈন্যদলের তালিকা দেখাইলেন এবং সৎ ও উচ্চমনা রাজা হইবার জন্য নানা উপদেশ দিলেন। শম্ভুজী পিতার কথা শুধু চুপ করিয়া শুনিয়া উত্তর দিলেন, "আপনার যাহা ইচ্ছা তাহাই হউক।” শিবাজী স্পষ্টই বুঝিলেন তাঁহার মৃত্যুর পর শম্ভুজীর হাতে মহারাষ্ট্র রাজ্যের কি দশা হইবে। এই দুর্ভাবনা ও হতাশা তাঁহার আয়ু হ্রাস করিল। শম্ভুজীকে আবার পনহালা-দুর্গে বন্দী করিয়া রাখা হইল, এবং শিবাজী রায়গড়ে ফিরিয়া আসিলেন (ফেব্রুয়ারি ১৬৮০)। তাঁহার দিন ফুরাইয়া আসিয়াছে বুঝিয়া, শিবাজী তাড়াতাডি কনিষ্ঠ পুত্র – দশ বৎসরের বালক রাজারামের উপবীত ও বিবাহ দিলেন (৭ই ও ১৫ই মার্চ)।
(সূত্র "শিবাজী" : যদুনাথ সরকার)

এখন এমন চরিত্রের মানুষ, যাকে তার পিতা পর্যন্ত ভরসা করেন নাই, দুইবার বন্দি করেছেন, দেশবাসী তাকে স্মরণ করে আহা উহু করবে, নাকি দেশের স্বাধীনতা আন্দোলনের বীর বিপ্লবী ক্ষুদিরাম, আসফাকুল্লাহ খান, সূর্য সেন, ভগৎ সিং, উধম সিং, সুভাষ চন্দ্র বসুর মত মানুষদের স্মরণ করে তাদের পথের পথিক হবে, তার ভাবনা সম্পূর্ণ তাদের উপরেই থাকল।

पैसे खर्च करके "छावा" देखना टाइम और पैसा दोनो बर्बाद करना है....।
जिस दृश्य को हम अपने गांव शहर में मुफ्त  में लाइव देख रहे हैं उसको फिल्म बनाकर बड़े पर्दे पर पैसे खर्च कर "छावा " देखने में क्या मतलब है? 
 'छावा' तो  ब्लैक एंड वाइट जमाने की फ़िल्म है डायरेक्टर ने तो इसे कलरफुल बना दिया है... पब्लिक लाल खून देखकर बेचैन हो रही है जबकि खून का रंग तो ब्लैक एंड वाइट के जमाने में भी लाल ही होता था......!

 ये फिल्म अफगान में 100 वर्षो से, पाक में 70 वर्षो से,बांग्लादेश में  लाइव धूम धड़ाके से चल रही है..... कश्मीर में 45 वर्ष पूर्व, संभल में 40 साल से, कैराना  में 25 साल से और दिल्ली वाले 4 वर्ष पहले ही इसका ट्रेलर देख भी चुके है....

₹500 खर्च करके छावा देखने से अच्छा है कि ₹100 की बिरयानी लेकर अब्दुल को अपने घर आमंत्रित कीजिए कुछ दिनों में छावा आपके घर पर खुद ही रिलीज हो जाएगी .......!
 शुभ भवतू।
वंदे मातरम।

snippet.textDisplay:
The Lion Cub, Chatrapati Shambaji made some mistakes. He didn't follow:
1. Escape plans, which were shown as live examples during his childhood by Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, who demonstrated sportiveness and secularism while hiding his masculinity and courage.
2. When he learned that 5000 people were attacking him, he should have planned and escaped, as his father did many times. It's well-known that a king's life doesn't belong to him; it belongs to his people. Fighting like a warrior against 5000 people was almost a suicide mission because one cannot handle hundreds of archers.
3. Chatrapati Shambaji blindly believed his family members. A king should always try to get secret information from secret agents. He didn't get any information even after the Mughals attacked.

We missed a lion cub at that time who could have achieved much more. However, he sacrificed himself without thinking about his people. Every Indian should take some time to think about Chatrapati Shambaji Maharaj and Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

Cinemas and stories like the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and the tales of Chatrapati Shivaji and Shambaji Maharaj never get boring. Directors should make more films on these subjects.

snippet.textDisplay:
The movie was quite good because its historical aspect and facts is deeply moving.

However, from an artistic point of view, Rashmika's casting was a big mistake. She neither spoke Hindi properly nor Marathi.

The costume and makeup artists did a great job.

In terms of direction, there were some inconsistencies in continuity.

When it comes to acting, Akshaye Khanna delivered an exceptional performance. Holding the screen with just pauses and dialogue, without relying on action, is a tough task, and he did it brilliantly.

As for the music, considering that A.R. Rahman composed it, it feels like it could have been even better.

There wasn’t a single Marathi folk element or war song, like Powada, which could have enhanced the storytelling and made it more impactful.

Perhaps incorporating both Marathi and Hindi elements would have made it even more immersive and enjoyable to listen to.

snippet.textDisplay:
1707- Aurangzeb Died in Maharashtra.
1718- Mughal Surrender in front of Balaji Viswanath Bhatt (Maratha Peshwa, Father of Legendary Baji Rao). Mughal Sign the treaty to pay taxes (Chauth, Sardeshmukhi) to Marathas.

1738- Mughal sign to become vassals of Maratha Peshwa Baji Rao. Marathas will dictate terms to Delhi Mughals.

1758- Marathas conquer most of present day subcontinent uptill Attock in present day Pakistan under Raghunath Rao. (Son of Baji Rao, brother of Nanasaheb Peshwa)

1788-  Mahadji Scindia (Legendary Maratha Sardaar) went to Delhi, tortured mughal throne occupier Ghulaam Qadir , blinded him and replaced him with Shah Alam 2nd. 


🙏🏻 These are facts with year-wise description.

snippet.textDisplay:
Amazing performance from the actors specially Vicky Kaushal, Akshay Khanna and Vineet Kumar. Great direction, good writing and excellent production from Maddock. Action sequences are very well crafted. AR Rehman's background music is solid. 

Movie is able showcase the valour of Sambhaji Maharaj and generates nationalism and pride in the audience. 
Only negative point I felt were scenes with Rashmika Mandhana. Those scenes were bit boring and kind of dampening the movie.
snippet.textOriginal:
Amazing performance from the actors specially Vicky Kaushal, Akshay Khanna and Vineet Kumar. Great direction, good writing and excellent production from Maddock. Action sequences are very well crafted. AR Rehman's background music is solid. 

Movie is able showcase the valour of Sambhaji Maharaj and generates nationalism and pride in the audience. 
Only negative point I felt were scenes with Rashmika Mandhana. Those scenes were bit boring and kind of dampening the movie.

snippet.textDisplay:
Some movies entertain, some educate, but only a rare few awaken something deep within the soul. Chhaava is not just a film—it is a feeling, a battle cry, a resonance of history that echoes through time.

From the very first frame, the film pulls you into the era of Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj, a warrior who stood unshaken in the face of tyranny. His story, buried under centuries of distortion, finds its voice through the powerful and electrifying portrayal by Vicky Kaushal. His performance is not just acting—it is a living embodiment of a ruler who gave his everything for Swarajya. His pain, his fire, his resilience—I felt every bit of it in my bones.

The visuals, the grand war sequences, the intricate detailing of Marathi culture, and the haunting background score—each element feels like a tribute to the sacrifices of our ancestors. The dialogues are not mere words; they are roars that stir the pride in every Indian’s heart.

But beyond its grandeur, Chhaava touched me on a deeply personal level. It made me reflect on the unbreakable spirit of those who came before us. The sacrifices, the betrayals, the bloodshed—it was never just history; it was a legacy we carry within us. And this film made me feel that legacy.

This is not just cinema. This is an experience. One that leaves your heart pounding, your eyes brimming, and your soul ignited with the fire of pride. Chhaava is a reminder that our history is not just meant to be remembered; it is meant to be lived.

I walked into the theatre as an audience, but I walked out as someone who felt the weight of history on my shoulders. And for that, I will forever be grateful to this film.

Jai Bhavani, Jai Shivaji! Jai Sambhaji!

snippet.textDisplay:
SAMBHAJI
1.Sambhaji was imprisoned  by his father at the Panhala because he "attempted to violate a Brahmin's wife , his addiction to alcohol.(, James W.  "Cracks in the Narrative". Shivaji: Hindu King in Islamic India. Oxford University Press. p. 93)
2.He served under Diler Khan in the Battle of Bhupalgarh against his father Shivaji.he was made a Mughal noble with the rank of seven thousand zat and conferred with the title of Raja by Aurangzeb.
Richards, John F. (1993). "Maratha insurgency and Mughal conquest in the Deccan".  Cambridge University Press. 

3.When Shivaji died on 5 April 1680, Sambhaji was still held captive at Panhala fort.
4.He imprisoned his step  brother Rajaram, his wife Janki Bai and his step mother Soyarabai for throne.

5.In 1683, he invaded Portuguese areas and  Goa, during which Maratha soldiers destroyed churches, raped Christian women and later sold captured men and women to Arabs and the Dutch. Marathas were notorious for gang-raping women during invasions, including the invasion of Goa under Sambhaji.They were so barbarous that when a woman appeared very beautiful (lit., best) to them, five or six of them violated her by lying with that woman alone, Up to now nowhere else in India has such barbarity been seen.For this reason, many women of Margaon ... threw themselves into pools, where they died of drowning
(Sarkar, Jadunath . Fall of the Mughal Empire. Vol. 1. Hyderabad: Orient Longman. p. 54-55.)

6.he had alienated deshmukhs by burning villages to deny supplies to the Portuguese. 
7.He gave shelter to Aurangzeb's son Akbar. Akber was hoping that Shambaji will help him against Aurangzeb but Shambhaji couldn't dare.

He insulted the emperor and the  prophet Muhammad PBUH during interrogation and was sentenced for attack on I'll prepared , Mughal garrison at burhanpur, they did plunder, killing, dishonour and torture against muslims in there for 3 days.
Aurangzeb ordered the execution of Sambhaji . Sambhaji's eyes were blinded and  behead on 11 March 1689 .Sambhaji's remains were fed to the dogs.

Fake hero. They were robbers.
Here is the English translation of the Bengali rhyme:  

**"The baby sleeps, the village rests,  
The Bargis have come to the land.  
The nightingales have eaten the paddy,  
How will we pay the tax?"**  

This rhyme reflects the historical context of the 18th century when the Maratha Bargis repeatedly raided Bengal, causing immense suffering to the villagers. It symbolizes the hardships faced by common people during that time.
এটি একটি জনপ্রিয় বাংলা ছড়ার প্রথম লাইন, যা ঐতিহাসিকভাবে মারাঠা বর্গীদের বাংলা আক্রমণের প্রসঙ্গ তুলে ধরে। ছড়াটি হলো:  

**খোকা ঘুমালো, পাড়া জুড়ালো,  
বর্গী এলো দেশে।  
বুলবুলিতে ধান খেয়েছে,  
খাজনা দেব কিসে?**

snippet.textDisplay: महाराष्ट्र में एक कहावत बेहद चर्चित है। कहा जाता है कि औरंगजेब ने संभाजी राजे की हत्या करने से ठीक पहले उनसे कहा था कि कि मेरे चार बेटों में से अगर एक भी तुम्हारे जैसा होता, तो पूरा हिंदुस्तान कब का मुगल सल्तनत में समा चुका होता। दरअसल, औरंगजेब के चारों बेटे योग्य नहीं थे। बताया जाता है कि संभाजी के शव के टुकड़े तुलापुर की नदी में फेंक दिए गए थे, जहां से निकालकर कुछ लोगों ने उनका अंतिम संस्कार किया था।

snippet.textDisplay: किताब के अनुसार, इस्लाम कबूलने से इनकार करने के बाद संभाजी राजे और उनके कवि व दोस्त कलश को जोकरों वाली पोशाक पहना कर पूरे शहरभर में परेड कराई गई। पूरे रास्ते उन पर पत्थरों की बरसात की गई। भाले चुभाए गए। उसके बाद उन्हें फिर से इस्लाम कबूलने के लिए कहा गया। फिर से इनकार करने पर और ज़्यादा यातनाएं दी गई। दोनों कैदियों की ज़ुबान कटवा दी गई। आंखें और निकाल लिए गए। इसके बाद उनके एक-एक अंग को काटा गया और आखिर में शरीर के कई टुकड़े कर दिए गए। इसके बाद भी औरंगजेब का मन नहीं भरा तो उसने 11 मार्च, 1689 को संभाजी के सिर को कलम कर दिया।

snippet.textDisplay:
Brief story of Sambhaji.

1. He was the eldest son of Shivaji, the founder of the Maratha Kingdom.
2. He was the second Chhatrapati of the Maratha Empire, ruling from 1681 to 1689.
3. His behaviour was very bad. He was addicted to sensual pleasures. Thus Shivaji imprison him at Panhala fort in 1678 to curb his behaviour.
4. When Shivaji died on 5 April 1680, Sambhaji was still held captive at Panhala fort.
5. He plotted his escape and took possession of the Panhala fort on 27 April after killing the fort commander.
6. He imprisoned his half brother Rajaram, his wife Janki Bai and mother Soyarabai.
7. He gave shelter to Aurangzeb's son Akbar. Akber was hoping tat Shambaji will help him against Aurangzeb but Shambhaji couldn't dare.
8. He executed 24 members of influential families including top government ministers in 1683.
9. He and 25 of his advisors were captured by the Mughal forces of Muqarrab Khan in a skirmish at Sangameshwar in February 1689.
10. He insulted the emperor and the  prophet Muhammad PBUH during interrogation and was executed for having killed Muslims.
The end.

Also..
It is not a film but a bundle of lies.
The film has been made on the basis of a fabricated story.  Whatever has been shown in this film is all nonsense, a lie. The reality is that the Marathas and the Mughals never fought face to face because the Maratha forces were weak and outnumbered. That is why the Marathas used to fight guerrilla wars.
The only battle they fought against the Mughals was the battle of Wai which they lost miserably.

snippet.textDisplay:
What was not shown in the movie...

Firstly, Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj was made to wear a taqta kulah (a cap worn to criminals in Iran). It was a multi-colored robe like that of a joker, with a heavy wooden cap on his head.

A heavy wooden block was placed around his neck, putting a great burden on it. His hands were bound to block. Bells were also tied to this block.

Heavy iron chains were placed on his hands and body.

Then, every moment, Maharaj and Kalash were tortured.

People around them were also inflicting pain. Pelting stones on maharaj and kavi kalash.

After that, Maharaj was paraded on a dwarf camel. Drums and other instruments played alongside. -Various forms of torture and humiliation were inflicted.

When sambhaji maharaj presented in the Darbar, he was covered in blood.

-Even after enduring such pain, Sambhaji Maharaj did not bow down before Aurangzeb. He roared on Aurangzeb.

That same night, hot iron rods were pushed into Maharaj's eyes, blinding him.

His hands were chopped off, and the poet Kalash's tongue was cut out.

After that, the proud Sambhaji Maharaj renounced the food.

For the next 15-20 days, Sambhaji Maharaj endured unimaginable torture.

His skin was peeled off.

Then, Sambhaji Maharaj's head was severed with a sword. After the head was separated, straw was stuffed into it, and it was displayed on a spear around the city.

Then, orderd to cut down sambhaji maharaj body in pieces.

-his mutilated body was thrown near tulapur.

There has probably never been a king in history who, like a mountain, embraced death with pride.

Despite the heart-wrenching torture, this king accepted death but never bowed to Aurangzeb... He chooses death and lot of torture. Our history is stained with the blood of such brave warriors. But remember it is not just a movie. It is the life of our ancestors who gave supreme sacrifice to protect Dharma and the nation. They embraced death over conversion and following adharma of the invader cults.

You & I are still living and following a dharma that is the oldest on the globe survived because of their sacrifices.

snippet.textOriginal:
What was not shown in the movie...

Firstly, Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj was made to wear a taqta kulah (a cap worn to criminals in Iran). It was a multi-colored robe like that of a joker, with a heavy wooden cap on his head.

A heavy wooden block was placed around his neck, putting a great burden on it. His hands were bound to block. Bells were also tied to this block.

Heavy iron chains were placed on his hands and body.

Then, every moment, Maharaj and Kalash were tortured.

People around them were also inflicting pain. Pelting stones on maharaj and kavi kalash.

After that, Maharaj was paraded on a dwarf camel. Drums and other instruments played alongside. -Various forms of torture and humiliation were inflicted.

When sambhaji maharaj presented in the Darbar, he was covered in blood.

-Even after enduring such pain, Sambhaji Maharaj did not bow down before Aurangzeb. He roared on Aurangzeb.

That same night, hot iron rods were pushed into Maharaj's eyes, blinding him.

His hands were chopped off, and the poet Kalash's tongue was cut out.

After that, the proud Sambhaji Maharaj renounced the food.

For the next 15-20 days, Sambhaji Maharaj endured unimaginable torture.

His skin was peeled off.

Then, Sambhaji Maharaj's head was severed with a sword. After the head was separated, straw was stuffed into it, and it was displayed on a spear around the city.

Then, orderd to cut down sambhaji maharaj body in pieces.

-his mutilated body was thrown near tulapur.

There has probably never been a king in history who, like a mountain, embraced death with pride.

Despite the heart-wrenching torture, this king accepted death but never bowed to Aurangzeb... He chooses death and lot of torture. Our history is stained with the blood of such brave warriors. But remember it is not just a movie. It is the life of our ancestors who gave supreme sacrifice to protect Dharma and the nation. They embraced death over conversion and following adharma of the invader cults.

You & I are still living and following a dharma that is the oldest on the globe survived because of their sacrifices.

They did not convert for power, money or other pleasures of life but laid down their lives for Dharma.

Jai Bhavani

Jai Shivaji

snippet.textDisplay:
It was great movie but I was looking for more accurate historical events. It was also hard to connect to other brave and wise characters and their contributions. Rashmika’s hindi was bit off but good try. Didn’t fully use versatile multitalented Akshay Khanna. Needed more expression and his other problems. Also needed natural light and less artificial lights. 
It felt like this movie was made to just show fighting, which was epic, never have I ever seen such realistic fight scene but I guess I was expecting a lot. I still remember there used to be serial name “Veer Shivaji,” which greatly influenced me and loved it a lot. So that was my reference point. But great try, we need more movies like this. 

Jay Bhavani, Jay Shivaji! Jay Shambhaji maharaj ji jay.

snippet.textDisplay:
Sambhaji, the son of the first Maratha King Shivaji, faced imprisonment during his father's reign due to his irresponsible behavior and indulgence in sensual pleasures. Shivaji took the step to arrest him, and kept him as a captive in Panhala fort. A theory suggests that the arrest of Sambhaji was caused due to his attempt to violate a Brahmin's wife.[2][3] Sambhaji managed to escape from the fort, and sought refuge with the Mughal forces under Diler Khan. However, he soon realized that Diler Khan intended to send him to Delhi as a prisoner, prompting Sambhaji to return. Upon his return, he was once again captured by the Marathas.[4][5]
After Shivaji's death, Sambhaji escaped from the Panhala fort and proclaimed himself king, eliminating all of Shivaji's ministers who opposed his succession.[6] Once on the throne, Sambhaji waged numerous campaigns against the Mughals, following in his father's footsteps. However, unlike Shivaji, he condoned the atrocities committed by his army. During his raid of Burhanpur, the inhabitants of the fort endured rape, torture, and robbery.

A theory suggests that the arrest of Sambhaji was caused due to his attempt to violate a Brahmin's wife.[2][3] Sambhaji managed to escape from the fort, and sought refuge with the Mughal forces under Diler Khan. However, he soon realized that Diler Khan intended to send him to Delhi as a prisoner, prompting Sambhaji to return. Upon his return, he was once again captured by the Marathas.[4][5]
After Shivaji's death, Sambhaji escaped from the Panhala fort and proclaimed himself king, eliminating all of Shivaji's ministers who opposed his succession.[6] Once on the throne, Sambhaji waged numerous campaigns against the Mughals, following in his father's footsteps. However, unlike Shivaji, he condoned the atrocities committed by his army. During his raid of Burhanpur, the inhabitants of the fort endured rape, torture, and robbery.

snippet.textDisplay:
Where the earth gives birth to heroes,
A lion roared there.
Son of Shivbaji, he was steadfast and true,
Sambhaji Maharaj, protector of Maratha.



Sword in hands, fire in heart,
Fought the Mughals, not a single stone wavered.
His morale was high even in captivity.
Gave everything, but did not leave religion.



Did not bow down even after suffering tortures,
Never stopped for Swarajya.
His sacrifice, an immortal story,
His voice echoes even today.



O brave Sambhaji, I bow to you,
Your bravery will remain immortal forever!
Pride of Marathas, pride of India,
May your name shine in the world!

-Aarush Korde 
13 yr old...

Imagine a young prince of 8 years age accompanied his great father to agra in 1666, to the very heart if Islamic invaders den. Fearless, despite knowing they might be attacked at any time.

Imagine the same prince losing his illustrious father when he was 22 and inheriting the burden of civilization itself in the form of Hindavi Swarajya of the ancient vedic people of Bharata, in 1680.

Imagine being surrounded by hostile Islamic invaders and a jihadi muinuddin setting on initial land of swarajya with 5 lakh hardened terrorists. Imagine the prince who became next chatrapati fighting against these odds and still denying the terrorists a victory from 1680 to 1687.

Imagine coordinating hundreds of battles, leading directly the forces in 150 battles and winning, averting the genocide of Hindus and standing like a rock against Islamic jihad.

Imagine the bravery and courage and grit to hold a enemy 100 times more powerful then you stuck in fighting you in vain and give breathing and reorganizing time to other Hindu forces across Bharat.

Imagine being backstabbing by his own family and getting captured by the same jihadis.

Being bound in chains, being insulted, being paraded and being surrounded by thousands of Islamic terrorists as they Leer abuse but still stand without fear.

Imagine being tortured in the worst possible way to give up the swarajya and hindutva and accept Islam and still roaring in the camp of the jihadi aurangzeb that ‘ I am son of chatrapati Shivaji and the head of swarajya that claims the land from uparisyena mountains to the Hindu ocean. The throne you sit on is mine, if you still surrender and atone for your sins, I may forgive you. No amount of land wealth or women can make me turn away from hindutva.” And going on to sing the shiv taandav strota at the face of these jihadis.

Tortured which cannot be described, tongue cutoff and when again he was asked if he will accept Islam, he asks for paper and pen and writing that his offer is the same.

Imagine being so courageous that even in the camp surrounded by thousands of terrorists, he was held up in iron chains of kilos since the terrorists knew that the tiger that chatrapati sambhaji was, he could have killed dozens of them even with his bare hands.

Dying by inhumane torture yet never gave up on his father's promise, on his mahadev, on his people and on this great ancient Bharat and inspiring millions in his death. Inspiring them to kill the dream of Islamic caliphate of the terrorist Aurangzeb

snippet.textDisplay: Being a Keralite, I regret that we haven't heard much about Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj or our Indian kings who fought and died for our land. Unfortunately, our NCERT textbooks presented only one side of the story, focusing mainly on the Mughals while omitting the atrocities committed by them. However, during my undergraduate studies in Maharashtra, I gained insight into how even  the younger generations there are aware of and deeply respect these kings. This experience made me realize that despite attempts to rewrite history, the truth will remain and live on through generations.
snippet.textOriginal: Being a Keralite, I regret that we haven't heard much about Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj or our Indian kings who fought and died for our land. Unfortunately, our NCERT textbooks presented only one side of the story, focusing mainly on the Mughals while omitting the atrocities committed by them. However, during my undergraduate studies in Maharashtra, I gained insight into how even  the younger generations there are aware of and deeply respect these kings. This experience made me realize that despite attempts to rewrite history, the truth will remain and live on through generations.

snippet.textDisplay:
There are many other great incidents about Chhatrapati Sambhaji and Shivaji Maharaj. That cannot be shown in this small 2.5-hour movie. If they include them, it will give us 2-3 more films. I have been watching many Marathi serials on Maharaj, and they took years and years to complete those small details. Although it's a great movie and a great try by Chhaava team. Thanks.

Some people say that they are producing this type of fake movies to spread hate. But as a Maharashtrian, I can confirm that this is our real history, and no one can think like this. We also have this history in our school books. We know this from decades. People from other states might have some doubts about this film. Even the tiger/lion scene is also real. If you find pictures of Ch.Sambhaji Maharaj on Google, you will get tiger pictures there.

Examples and sources -

Serials

1) Raje ShivChhatrapati 

2) Swarajya Rakshak Sambhaji Maharaj 

Movies - 

Marathi Chhaava 

Paavankhind

Farzand 

Har har mahadev 

Tanhaji 

Books - 

Chhaava - Shivaji Sawant 

SSC board history books -specially primary school.

Jay Bhawani Jay Shivaji/Sambhaji( Raaje) 🔥

Movie me bahut kuch he but bahut kuch baki bhi he.
